senses.gloss: To make full use of a resource or an opportunity.
examples: The company plans to *exploit* the new oil field.
She *exploited* every weakness in her opponent's defense.
Farmers here have been *exploiting* solar power for years.

senses.gloss: To examine an idea or a possibility carefully in order to see what it offers.
examples: We should *explore* other options before we decide.
The report *explored* the causes of the shortage.
They are *exploring* a merger with a smaller bank.

senses.gloss: To save data out of a program in a form that another program can open.
examples: You can *export* the table as a CSV file.
I *exported* my contacts to a spreadsheet.
The chart has already been *exported* to PDF.

senses.gloss: To offer or give something formally, such as an invitation, thanks, or credit.
examples: Let me *extend* a warm welcome to our guests.
The mayor *extended* his condolences to the family.
An invitation has been *extended* to every member of the club.

senses.gloss: To pull something out with effort, or to get a substance out of a plant or the ground.
examples: The dentist had to *extract* two teeth.
She *extracted* a splinter from his thumb with tweezers.
Oil is *extracted* from the seeds by pressing them.

senses.gloss: To get information, money, or a promise out of someone who does not want to give it.
examples: Detectives spent all night trying to *extract* a confession.
He *extracted* a promise that she would call before midnight.
The statement was *extracted* under pressure and later thrown out.

senses.gloss: To invent a story or evidence in order to deceive people.
examples: He had to *fabricate* an excuse on the spot.
The witness *fabricated* the whole story.
The emails were *fabricated* to make her look guilty.

senses.gloss: To stop working the way it should.
senses.ru: отказывать, отказать; выходить из строя, переставать работать
examples: The brakes *failed* halfway down the hill.
If the power *fails*, the generator starts automatically.
Doctors told him his kidneys were *failing*.

senses.gloss: To judge a student's work as not good enough to pass.
examples: The professor *failed* half the class.
They'll *fail* you if you skip the final.
She was *failed* for copying someone else's answers.

senses.gloss: To find something wrong with someone or with what they have done.
senses.ru: винить, обвинять; упрекать, ставить в вину
examples: You can't *fault* her for trying.
Nobody *faulted* his decision to leave early.
The report has been *faulted* for leaving out the costs.

senses.gloss: To have something as an important or attractive part.
examples: The apartment *features* hardwood floors and a large balcony.
The older model *featured* a headphone jack.
It's a small hotel *featuring* a rooftop pool and a garden.

senses.gloss: To fight with a long thin sword as a sport.
examples: She learned to *fence* in college.
They *fenced* for an hour every morning.
He has been *fencing* since he was ten.

senses.gloss: To join a male cell with an egg so that a young animal or plant can begin to grow.
examples: Bees *fertilize* the blossoms in spring.
Only one sperm actually *fertilized* the egg.
The eggs are *fertilized* outside the body and then implanted.

senses.gloss: To be sold for a particular price.
examples: The painting could *fetch* two million dollars.
His old guitar *fetched* far more than he expected.
Beach houses here have *fetched* record prices this year.

senses.gloss: To deal with questions or calls one after another as they come in.
examples: The coach *fielded* questions for twenty minutes.
She *fields* about fifty calls a day.
He was *fielding* complaints all morning.

senses.gloss: To put a team, a candidate, or a group of people forward to take part in something.
examples: The party will *field* a candidate in every district.
They *fielded* their strongest team in years.
The school has never *fielded* a girls' hockey team before.

senses.gloss: To smooth or shape something by rubbing it with a rough metal tool.
examples: She stopped to *file* a broken nail.
He *filed* the edge of the key until it fit the lock.
The weld has been *filed* smooth.

senses.gloss: To walk somewhere in a line, one person behind another.
senses.ru: идти вереницей, проходить гуськом; выстраиваться цепочкой
examples: The students *filed* into the auditorium.
We watched the jurors *file* silently to their seats.
Mourners were *filing* past the casket all afternoon.

senses.gloss: To put someone into a job or a position that is empty.
examples: They still haven't *filled* the manager's job.
The position was *filled* internally.
We're *filling* two openings this month.

senses.gloss: To supply what a customer has ordered or a doctor has prescribed.
examples: The pharmacy can *fill* your prescription in ten minutes.
They *filled* the order the same day.
That prescription has already been *filled* once.

senses.gloss: To move slowly and in small amounts through or into a place.
examples: Sunlight *filtered* through the blinds.
News of the layoffs *filtered* through the office by noon.
Voices from the hallway kept *filtering* into the room.

senses.gloss: To shoot a gun, or to launch a weapon.
examples: Don't *fire* until I give the signal.
The officer *fired* two warning shots.
Missiles were *fired* from a ship offshore.

senses.gloss: To bake clay in a very hot oven so that it hardens.
examples: We'll *fire* the kiln on Saturday.
She *fired* her first bowl last weekend.
These tiles are *fired* at 2,200 degrees.

senses.gloss: To prepare food or a drink for someone.
examples: Let me *fix* you a sandwich.
He *fixed* himself a cup of coffee.
She was *fixing* dinner when the phone rang.

senses.gloss: To decide something definitely, such as a date, a price, or a limit.
examples: They *fixed* the wedding date for June 12.
The rent is *fixed* for the first two years.
The committee will *fix* a deadline next week.

senses.gloss: To arrange a game, a race, or an election dishonestly so that a particular side wins.
examples: Someone had *fixed* the fight.
They tried to *fix* the election in three counties.
The match was *fixed*, and two players went to prison.

senses.gloss: To lose strength, energy, or interest.
senses.ru: ослабевать, ослабеть; выдыхаться; идти на спад
examples: Attendance began to *flag* after the first week.
Her enthusiasm never *flagged*.
Sales have been *flagging* since spring.

senses.gloss: To let someone down by not doing what you promised, especially by not showing up.
examples: Don't *flake* — we've been planning this for weeks.
He *flaked* again and never showed up.
I thought she had *flaked*, but she was just stuck in traffic.

senses.gloss: To become wider toward the bottom or the end.
examples: These jeans *flare* slightly at the ankle.
Her nostrils *flared* with anger.
She wore a long skirt *flaring* from the waist down.

senses.gloss: To break out suddenly, said of anger, violence, or an illness.
senses.ru: вспыхивать, вспыхнуть (о конфликте, гневе); обостряться, обостриться
examples: Tempers *flared* during the last quarter.
His arthritis *flares* whenever the weather turns.
Fighting has *flared* along the border again.

senses.gloss: To show something to someone for just a moment.
examples: Just *flash* your ticket at the door.
He *flashed* his badge and walked past the desk.
She kept *flashing* a grin at the camera.

senses.gloss: To make someone look more attractive than they usually do.
senses.ru: быть к лицу, идти (об одежде, причёске); выгодно подчёркивать
examples: That color really *flatters* you.
The old photograph *flattered* him.
This lighting isn't *flattering* anyone.

senses.gloss: To toss a coin in the air in order to decide something by chance.
examples: Let's *flip* a coin for it.
The referee *flipped* the coin at midfield.
They're *flipping* a coin to see who goes first.

senses.gloss: To buy something cheaply and resell it quickly for a profit.
examples: They *flip* houses for a living.
He *flipped* the tickets for twice what he paid.
She's been *flipping* thrift-store furniture on the side.

senses.gloss: To suggest an idea in order to see how people react to it.
senses.ru: выдвигать (идею на пробу), предлагать; закидывать удочку
examples: Let me *float* an idea past the team.
She *floated* the possibility of a four-day week.
His name has been *floated* as a possible replacement.

senses.gloss: To arrive somewhere in overwhelming numbers, or to send something in overwhelming numbers.
senses.ru: хлынуть, нахлынуть; заваливать, завалить (звонками, товаром); наводнять
examples: Calls *flooded* the station after the broadcast.
Cheap imports have *flooded* the market.
Volunteers kept *flooding* into the shelter all weekend.

senses.gloss: To shock or amaze someone completely.
examples: The news absolutely *floored* me.
I was *floored* when they offered me the job.
Her answer is going to *floor* you.

senses.gloss: To press a car's gas pedal all the way down.
senses.ru: жать на газ до упора, вдавить педаль в пол
examples: He *floored* it and shot through the intersection.
Don't *floor* the gas on wet pavement.
She was *flooring* it the whole way home.

senses.gloss: To turn red in the face from heat, embarrassment, or strong feeling.
examples: She *flushed* when he read her name out loud.
His face *flushes* whenever he has to speak in public.
Her cheeks were *flushed* from the cold.

senses.gloss: To adjust a camera or your eyes so that what you see is sharp.
senses.ru: наводить резкость, фокусировать, сфокусировать; фокусироваться (о зрении)
examples: Let me *focus* the camera before you move.
He *focused* the binoculars on the far shore.
Her eyes wouldn't *focus* after the drops.

senses.gloss: To close down because of losing money.
examples: The magazine *folded* after twelve years.
Three restaurants on this block have *folded* since March.
If the grant doesn't come through, the program will *fold*.

senses.gloss: To stop playing your hand in a card game and give up the round.
examples: She looked at her cards and decided to *fold*.
I *folded* before the last card.
He should have *folded* early and saved his chips.

senses.gloss: To do what an instruction, a rule, or a recipe tells you to do.
examples: Just *follow* the directions on the box.
She *followed* the recipe exactly.
The crew has been *following* safety procedures to the letter.

senses.gloss: To understand what someone is saying.
senses.ru: понимать, улавливать (мысль); следить за ходом мысли
examples: Sorry, I don't *follow*.
Nobody *followed* his explanation of the tax rules.
Are you *following* me so far?

senses.gloss: To keep up with news about a person, a team, or a subject.
senses.ru: следить за (новостями, командой); подписаться (на кого-л. в соцсетях)
examples: I don't really *follow* baseball.
She *followed* the trial closely.
Thousands of people are *following* the account.

senses.gloss: To open something by breaking it or by using physical strength.
examples: They had to *force* the door to get her out.
Someone *forced* the lock on the shed.
The window had been *forced* from the outside.

senses.gloss: To make an illegal copy of a document, a signature, or money.
examples: He tried to *forge* his father's signature.
She *forged* the prescription and got caught at the pharmacy.
The passport had been expertly *forged*.

senses.gloss: To build a strong relationship or agreement through effort.
examples: The two countries are trying to *forge* a trade deal.
She *forged* close ties with local businesses.
It was a friendship *forged* during the worst year of the war.

senses.gloss: To set up an organization, a group, or a partnership.
examples: We plan to *form* a nonprofit next year.
The band *formed* in Austin in 2009.
A new government is being *formed* this week.

senses.gloss: To develop an idea, an opinion, or a habit in your mind.
examples: Try not to *form* an opinion before you hear both sides.
He *formed* the habit of walking after dinner.
I was still *forming* an impression of the place.

senses.gloss: To prepare a disk or a memory card for use, erasing everything on it.
examples: You'll need to *format* the drive first.
I accidentally *formatted* the wrong card.
The laptop has been *formatted* and reinstalled twice.

senses.gloss: To add vitamins or minerals to a food or a drink.
examples: Most milk sold here is *fortified* with vitamin D.
They *fortified* the flour with iron and folic acid.
The program *fortifies* salt with iodine.

senses.gloss: To take a child or an animal into your home and care for them for a time without adopting them.
senses.ru: брать на воспитание (в приёмную семью); приютить (животное)
examples: They *fostered* three kids before adopting one of them.
Would you consider *fostering* a dog for a few weeks?
She has *fostered* more than twenty children.

senses.gloss: To make air, water, or a surface dirty.
examples: Runoff from the plant *fouled* the river.
Smoke from the fires *fouls* the air for weeks.
The beach had been *fouled* by oil from the tanker.

senses.gloss: To break apart into rival groups because of disagreement.
examples: The party *fractured* over the budget.
Years of argument have *fractured* the movement.
The coalition is *fracturing* along regional lines.

senses.gloss: To make an innocent person appear guilty by arranging false evidence.
senses.ru: подставлять, подставить; ложно обвинить, сфабриковать дело против
examples: He says the police *framed* him.
Someone was trying to *frame* her for the theft.
He spent nine years in prison after being *framed*.

senses.gloss: To present an issue in a particular way so that people see it as you want.
examples: It depends on how you *frame* the question.
The campaign *framed* the vote as a choice about jobs.
The debate is being *framed* as a fight over spending.
